question.value: When in cosmic history did the distinct internal structures of spiral galaxies (stellar bulge, rotating disk, and spiral arms) form, and are they present in an intensely star-forming galaxy at z = 4.41?

evidence.quote: Spiral galaxies have distinct internal structures including a stellar bulge, disk and spiral arms. It is unknown when in cosmic history these structures formed. We analyze observations of BRI 1335-0417, an intensely star-forming galaxy in the distant Universe, at redshift 4.41.
The ALMA pipeline calibrated data and raw data are available at http://almascience.nrao.edu/aq/ under project code ADS/JAO.ALMA #2017.1.00394.S.
At the redshift for BRI 1335-0417 of _z_ = 4.4074 ( _11_ ), the [C II ] line of 1900.5369 GHz is shifted to 351.470 GHz and can be observed with ALMA Band 7 (275 – 373 GHz)

analysis_steps.goal: 3D gas dynamical modeling of bulge and disk masses

method.value: Generate gas particles from CLEAN components using SkySampler, build 3D dynamical model cubes in KinMS with a spherical de Vaucouleurs bulge + thick pressure-supported exponential disk gravitational potential, and fit directly to the observed cube via MCMC using emcee.

evidence.quote: We used the K IN MS code ( _40_ ) to produce a gas dynamical model cube which has the same beam size and velocity resolution as those in the observed cube (i.e. beam smearing effect was taken into account for the model cube).

findings_qualitative.value: BRI 1335-0417 exhibits a two-armed spiral morphology in [C II] extending from 2 to 5 kpc in radius, already formed at z = 4.41 (1.4 Gyr after the Big Bang).

evidence.quote: The [C II ] gas kinematics show a steep velocity rise near the galaxy center and have a two-armed spiral morphology that extends from about 2 to 5 kiloparsecs in radius.
These features had been formed within 1.4 billion years after the Big Bang, long before the peak of cosmic star formation.

findings_qualitative.value: No evidence of a bipolar outflow is found in [C II] line emission, unlike what was previously reported in CO (J=7->6).

evidence.quote: In addition, in [C II ] line emission, we could not find any evidence of bipolar outflow which is reported in CO ( _J_ =7→6) line ( _14_ ).

claims.hypothesis: Distinct internal structures of spiral galaxies—a central compact bulge-like structure, a rotating disk, and spiral arms—can already exist at z = 4.41 (1.4 Gyr after the Big Bang).
claims.experiment: Image archival ALMA Band 7 [C II] and dust continuum observations of BRI 1335-0417 at ~0.17"-0.20" resolution and decompose the deprojected [C II] intensity using logarithmic spiral Fourier modes.
claims.result: A two-armed (m = 2) spiral structure extending from 2 to 5 kpc is detected at SNR = 6.0 with a pitch angle of 26.7 (+4.1/-1.6)°, embedded in a near-exponential [C II] disk (n = 0.87 ± 0.02, R_d = 1.83 ± 0.04 kpc) and centrally concentrated dust continuum (n = 2.48 ± 0.05).
claims.finding: Spiral arms (or tidal features), a rotating disk, and a central compact structure had already formed within 1.4 billion years after the Big Bang.

evidence.quote: The [C II ] gas kinematics show a steep velocity rise near the galaxy center and have a two-armed spiral morphology that extends from about 2 to 5 kiloparsecs in radius.
These features had been formed within 1.4 billion years after the Big Bang, long before the peak of cosmic star formation.
The amplitude of the _m_ =2 signal is 6.0 times the noise, while the other modes _m_ =1, 3, 4 are have signal-to-noise ratios of 4.0, 2.5 and 2.4 respectively (Fig. 3A).

claims.hypothesis: The [C II] gas disk of BRI 1335-0417 is rotation-dominated and gravitationally unstable in its outer regions.
claims.experiment: Extract the major-axis PVD and velocity dispersion profile to measure v_rot / sigma_v, and compute the spatially resolved Toomre Q parameter across the disk.
claims.result: v_rot = 179 (+25/-18) km s^-1, sigma_v = 71 (+14/-11) km s^-1, giving v_rot / sigma_v = 2.5 (+0.6/-0.4), and Toomre Q < 1 at R > 0.2".
claims.finding: The gas disk is rotation-dominated and gravitationally unstable in the outer parts, making it susceptible to star formation and spontaneous spiral structure formation.

evidence.quote: 2.5 -0.4 indicates that the [C II ] gas disk of this galaxy is rotation-dominated.

We find _Q_ is less than 1 throughout the outer part of the disk (Fig. S6), indicating the gas disk is susceptible to gravitational collapse, star formation ( _7_ – _9_ ) and spontaneous formation of spiral structure ( _3_, _24_ ).

claims.hypothesis: The steep central velocity rise in BRI 1335-0417 is driven by a massive central compact structure (bulge and/or supermassive black hole) plus an extended gas disk.
claims.experiment: Perform 3D forward dynamical modeling of the [C II] cube with KinMS and MCMC sampling (emcee) using a spherical de Vaucouleurs bulge + exponential disk gravitational potential.
claims.result: The central compact mass is 8.9 (+20.9/-3.7) x 10^9 M_sun (5.2 x 10^9 to 3.0 x 10^10 M_sun) with R_e < 1.33 kpc, and the disk mass is 4.9 (+1.7/-2.5) x 10^10 M_sun.
claims.finding: The kinematics require a central compact mass compatible with local stellar bulges or the previously estimated ~6 x 10^9 M_sun black hole, alongside a gas disk whose dynamical mass matches the CO-derived molecular gas mass.

evidence.quote: The best-fitting effective radius of the compact structure _R_ e is less than 1.3kpc (at 95% confidence interval) and its mass is 5.2 × 10 [9] to 3.0 × 10 [10] _M_ ⨀ depending on the value of _R_ e .
mass of the disk 4.9 -2.5 × 10 _M_ ⨀ is consistent with the molecular gas mass of 5.1 × 10 _M_ ⨀ ( _16_ ) estimated from the CO ( _J_ =2→1) luminosity

why_this_data.value: Previous [C II] observations had insufficient spatial resolution to determine the gas distribution and kinematics, whereas the archival Band 7 C43-5 data resolve the galaxy at ~1.3 kpc.

evidence.quote: [C II ] line emission from this object was detected in previous observations at lower spatial resolution, insufficient to determine the gas

why_this_method.value: Direct 3D cube modeling with KinMS accounts for beam smearing, pressure support (asymmetric drift) accounts for the high velocity dispersion, and scaling delta chi^2 by sqrt(2N) prevents unrealistically small MCMC confidence intervals from ~4 x 10^4 constraints.

evidence.quote: We used the K IN MS code ( _40_ ) to produce a gas dynamical model cube which has the same beam size and velocity resolution as those in the observed cube (i.e. beam smearing effect was taken into account for the model cube).

evidence.loc: Rotation velocity of pressurized galactic disk
evidence.quote: The pressure in the gas disk is proportional to the square of the velocity dispersions of the gas, which is not negligible for the gas dynamical modeling ( _61_ ).

In our data ( _N_ ~ 4 ´ 10 [4] and _O_ = 8), it becomes 2 _N_ and yields an unrealistically small confidence interval due to the large number of constraints in fitting the observed cube. We used a method of scaling the standard Dc [2] by a factor of,(2 _N_ ) ( _68_ ).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Tidal-tail origin from a major merger for the two-armed morphology is disfavored (as tidal tails typically occur on >10 kpc scales, whereas these arms are <5 kpc and connected to the rotating disk), though not completely ruled out.

evidence.quote: Tidal-tail features in a galaxy merger are expected occur on larger scales (>10kpc) ( _6_, _31_ ). We therefore disfavor, but cannot completely rule out, a tidal-tail origin for the observed spiral morphology.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Dark matter halo component in the dynamical model was excluded because [C II] is detected only out to 5 kpc, where baryons dominate.

evidence.quote: In this object, the [C II ] line emission is detected only up to 5 kpc, which is not sufficient to measure the mass distribution of the dark matter using the kinematics. We therefore excluded the dark matter mass distribution from our dynamical model.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Bipolar outflow kinematics were excluded from dynamical modeling because no outflow signature was detected in the [C II] spectrum.

evidence.quote: We could not find any evidence of bipolar outflow in [C II ] line emission, but this does not exclude the bipolar outflow seen in CO ( _J_ =7→6) line emission because the [C II ] line may not be strongly emitted from the outflowing material.
Therefore, we did not consider the outflow kinematics in the gas dynamical modeling.

limitations_admitted.value: Spatial resolution (~0.2") is much larger than the black hole sphere of influence (0.02"), so the black hole mass and stellar bulge mass cannot be separated dynamically (allowing a black hole without a bulge).

evidence.quote: Because estimated _R_ SOI is much smaller than our spatial resolution, we cannot measure the circular velocity of black hole _v_ BH ( _r_ ) and bulge _v_ bulge ( _r_ ) separately. We thus included the black hole mass in the bulge.

limitations_admitted.value: Gas inflow into the galaxy center driven by spiral torques cannot be directly detected due to limited signal-to-noise ratio.

evidence.quote: Such gas inflow could not be directly detected in our data due to the limited signal to noise ratio.

limitations_admitted.value: Pixel-to-pixel covariance matrix correction in the data cube was omitted because it is negligible compared to the sqrt(2N) log-likelihood scaling.

evidence.quote: The correction by the inverse covariance matrix for the pixel to pixel correlations ( _71_ ) in the observed data cube is not taken into account, because it is negligible compared to the effect by scaling the logarithmic likelihood.

referee_caveats_inferred: Distinguishing genuine density-wave/bar-driven spiral arms from merger-induced tidal arms or streams at ~1.3 kpc resolution remains morphological and somewhat degenerate.

Disk inclination is inferred from the dust continuum axis ratio assuming an axisymmetric thin disk (q = cos i), even though the dust continuum has a high Sérsic index (n = 2.48) and non-axisymmetric bar-like features.
The sqrt(2N) chi-square scaling is an ad-hoc heuristic to inflate uncertainties in correlated interferometric cubes rather than a full visibility-plane or covariance-matrix treatment.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~10-30 GB for the raw and calibrated visibility dataset (1 execution block, 2 hours total, Band 7 with two 1920-channel and two 128-channel spectral windows); < 50 MB for supplementary FITS cubes S1-S4.
reproducibility.score_reason: Archival ALMA project code is stated and public, processed FITS cubes and model cubes are directly included as supplementary data (Data S1-S4), and the CASA imaging, Fourier spiral decomposition, and KinMS+emcee dynamical modeling equations, priors, and settings are thoroughly documented.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public single-project ALMA dataset (2017.1.00394.S) with a complete, well-specified analysis recipe and clear quantitative targets (spiral pitch angle, v_rot/sigma_v, and dynamical bulge/disk masses).
